[lanes: correctness, api-contract]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: register.js:225-242 `ackIds()` groups ids only by `via` and `doAck` passes the whole group; `retryAcks()` (:278) feeds it `Object.keys(S.rec.unacked)` with no cap. src/cli/watch.rs `run_ack_lines` sends all remote ids in one `AckModDelivered` and on any non-`ModDeliveryAcked` result does `return 1` with no output. src/protocol/commands.rs:810 `MAX_BATCH_ITEMS = 100`; :958-967 rejects `ack.messages.len() > MAX_BATCH_ITEMS`; src/store/receipts.rs:131/:245 reject `len() > 100` again. `doAck` then marks every id `retryable`, so each retry resends the same oversized batch. `pump()` submits the whole non-lazy queue as one batch and the registration drain streams everything pending, so a backlog over 100 produces this. No chunking test exists (tests/cli/watch.rs "chunk" hits are body-chunk reassembly).
  fix-shape hint: chunk ids to at most 100 per `watch ack` call in `doAck`/`ackIds`, or have `run_ack_lines` split into multiple `AckModDelivered` calls and merge the reports; add a test with 101+ ids.

- [Should-fix] src/cli/watch.rs:340 — A transient failure of the Capabilities call (admission full, timeout, daemon still booting) is reported as `unsupported`, which exits 3, and the mod then stops watching for the rest of the Claude session. [lanes: premortem]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: src/cli/watch.rs:340-344 `run_session` returns `refuse(.., Unsupported)` when `supports_capability(MOD_WATCH, ..)` is false, before `open_watch` (the only place `DaemonUnavailable`, exit 2, can arise). src/client/local.rs:52-58 `capabilities()` maps every call error to `Capabilities::none()` (`_ => Capabilities::none()`). src/protocol/watch.rs:306 maps `Unsupported` to `WATCH_EXIT_STOP` (3). register.js:131-135 `if (code === 3) { S.stopped = true; return }`; the tick at :501 restarts only when `!S.stopped`; only `onSessionEnd` (:463) resets it. src/daemon/transport.rs:202 drops accepted connections when the 32 `MAX_CONNECTIONS` permits are taken. The design exit table (design.md:120-127) reserves exit 3 for a genuinely unsupported daemon and maps an unreachable or busy daemon to exit 1/2 (retry with backoff). The `Capabilities::none()`-on-error mapping existed on base (08cea709 local.rs:56) but only fed optional features; this change is the first consumer that turns it into a permanent stop.
  fix-shape hint: make the probe distinguish "call failed" from "answered without `mod.watch_v1`" (e.g. `capabilities()` returning `Result`/`Option`), and map transport or timeout errors to `DaemonUnavailable` (exit 2) so the mod retries with backoff.

[lanes: concurrency-async]

Self-heals: the mod reconnects after backoff and RebindGrace counts as live; cost is one spurious Close and possible at-least-once redelivery.
  fix-shape hint: pass the snapshot generation (or channel id) into `close()` and return early under the lock if the entry no longer matches, mirroring `observe_fingerprint`.

[lanes: concurrency-async]

  fix-shape hint: have `stalled()` return the channel id / `connected_since` it judged, and have `close(Stalled)` verify them under the lock before removing the entry and arming the cooldown.

Rejected 0-3: design D2 (:100) states last-writer-wins ("A second watch for the same seat and generation replaces the first"); `stopChild()`/`startChild()` bump `S.run` so an old watcher's exit 3 is ignored (register.js:126); the inverted order needs a daemon delay longer than a fresh process spawn and no evidence shows it; the stop lasts only until `session.end`/`session.start`. The exit-3-for-`replaced` mapping is already tracked as code-final-review-1 F5.
- integrations/claude/mod/hooks/register.js:18 — `frame()` interpolates peer bodies raw with no escaping or per-line prefix. Rejected 2-1: roast-design-1.md:103 rejected "Forged header lines inside a body" 2-1 under the cooperative model, noting JSON-encoding the body as "not material"; AGENTS.md/TRUST-POLICY forbid adversarial hardening; the HEADER already marks the block untrusted; `escape_for_terminal` protects a human terminal, a different threat. Dissent noted: the reproduce seat confirmed at Should-fix citing design D4 "matching the hook's `untrusted_peer_data` convention" (hook.rs:524,781 uses an escaped JSON container) and the CLI design doc :70; the majority's roast citation covers that exact point. Survives as a Nit-level hardening idea: JSON-encode or prefix bodies and sender/thread to close the invisible Unicode tag-character channel.

Rejected 2-1: the refute and ground seats disprove the premise. src/store/attention.rs:30-36 defines the digest "warnings" class to include programmatic service notices (`digest_programmatic_warnings`), so `ModFingerprint.other_pending` (seats.rs:4355) counts them and `has_pending()` turns true; InboxBatchV2 `Source::Warnings` (queries.rs ~6190-6207) emits `Item::Warning` gated on `informational_notice_pending`, so `drain()` (watch.rs:497) sets `saw_attention` and emits the `attention` line. The reproduce seat said it did not check the fingerprint claim. - integrations/claude/mod/hooks/register.js:449; :332 — `onSessionEnd` bumps `S.gen` while a submit/append is pending, so a successful in-flight delivery is submitted again after resume. Rejected 2-1: at-least-once across a handoff is an accepted limit (design.md:259, :320; TRUST-POLICY "/branch" text; mod README ~:105); the `gen !== S.gen` drop is deliberate ("a resolution from before a session change touches nothing"); the failure is a duplicate, never a loss. - integrations/claude/mod/hooks/register.js:673 — `session.start` replaces the core while the old core's chains still run, so two cores can write `delivered:<sid>`. Rejected 0-3: needs a second `session.start` with in-flight work in the same core; real session changes go through `session.end` and `refresh()`; the worst case is a duplicate the README Persistence section accepts; acks are idempotent.
- integrations/claude/mod/hooks/register.js:217; :221 — The context-path ack is queued as a microtask before `onToolCall` returns. Rejected 0-3: design D6 defines the delivered predicate as the hook returning the answered result with the context entry, which the code checks (:444-453); "an outer mod could strip context after the hook returned" is a listed accepted limit; no evidence the engine discards a returned context; a hook cannot observe engine consumption after returning.
- src/service/mod_channels.rs:249 — Every commit on 18 tables re-runs `mod_seat_view` for every live channel. Rejected 0-3: documented design (`MOD_NOTIFY_TABLES` doc, spec D2); runs on the dedicated `herdr-mod-channels` thread, never on the commit path; the dirty flag coalesces bursts; bounded by 64 channels and 1001-row digest caps; no stated latency requirement.

Rejected 2-1: the read happens only for a mod-live seat 10+ minutes without an ack with a push on record; 1 s is a timeout cap on a local read; D7 requires a stalled channel to stop suppressing immediately, so the scheduler must ask; the wake worker is single-threaded.
